parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction: no trans-specific offence, no documented enforcement, violence, or police practice against trans people — but also no monitoring, so silence is not safety. No LGR and no marker-change procedure means a document-mismatch traveller carries the discrepancy into every border, immigration and hotel check with no domestic remedy; that is a recurring outing vector, though no source documents officials reacting badly to it. The only protections (labour-code discrimination ban, SO hate-crime sentencing enhancement) name sexual orientation, not gender identity, and reach neither services nor visitors reliably. Broad LGBTQ stigmatisation is documented but not trans-specific. Extrapolating per the thin-data rule: decriminalising code, no relief mechanisms, no protective infrastructure, general stigma — but no criminal statute aimed at expression and no documented hostility reaching travellers. This sits between the 0.65-C profile (documented acceptance with dead-letter law) and the 0.45 tier (no universal-exposure rule documented, but no documented acceptance either). Friction and unresolved document handling, without documented targeting or remedy, place it in Elevated Risk at roughly 0.55.
